reviewer: /root/transformer_runtime_audit (independent source, operation-count and exact theorem-type review)
scope: The same exact Transformer DC split-streams admit a materialized shared evaluation whose explicitly accumulated real-arithmetic counter is at most 200 times SharedRuntime.networkSize. The endpoint also retains exact output recovery, convexity and nonnegativity of both heads, coordinatewise monotonicity on independent nonnegative inputs, and globally convex raw-input heads. The architecture has arbitrary finite depth and the existing Transformer type hypotheses.
findings: The independent audit driver spells out the full contract rather than merely checking a theorem name; the successful Lean log prints that exact type and the proof term.

The combined endpoint proves equality of BOTH computed shared heads to net.decompose, not merely equality of their difference. TransformerSharedCorrectness supplies this bridge stage by stage and through arbitrary block lists.

Costed binds cache their left result. gather first materializes Vector.ofFn f once, then reads cached values and counters; the earlier duplicate f invocation was corrected before the successful build.
The shared evaluator materializes Q/K/V projections, attention rows, normalization intermediates and block outputs. It does not evaluate the expanded recursive Expr tree.

All input-dependent scalar arithmetic in the split kernels is explicitly charged. Manual counts agree with checked counts: constPair 3, addPair 2, scalePair 4, mulPair 12, sumPair 2n; GELU 15, Swish 18, sigmoid 17, softplus 7, ReLU 1; whole-row softmax 8n+4; whole-token LayerNorm 39n+18; inverse-root pair 6 in either branch, including the comparison.

networkSize is an independent size of a conventional shared ordinary forward graph, including constant nodes, affine projections, score products, row softmax, Value aggregation, output projections, norms, residuals, MLPs and readout. It is not defined as a multiple of split work.

The cost proof first derives exact stage counters or bounds from the actual shared evaluator, then compares their structural aggregation with networkSize. No assumed runtime certificate, size bound or decomposition certificate is a theorem hypothesis.

The universal constant 200 is conservative and independent of token count, feature dimensions, number of heads, finite block depth and input values. networkSize includes attention arithmetic for the chosen sequence length; this is not a linear-in-sequence-length claim.

The manuscript cost equation is inside the Transformer theorem and explicitly uses shared values and unit-cost arithmetic, comparisons and scalar activation/special-function evaluations. The old correctness, convexity and monotonicity conclusions remain intact.
No new axiom, sorry, unsafe theorem shortcut or sorryAx was found. The printed axiom audit for both the combined endpoint and its semantic bridge uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

cost_model.unit_cost: Real arithmetic, comparisons, exp, log, Gaussian CDF and fixed-power evaluation; the rpow kernel is used at exponent -1/2.
cost_model.preprocessing: Fixed model/dimension constants, including the Gaussian density normalization, LayerNorm inverse-root slope and epsilon power, and softmax dimension normalization, are precomputed parameters.
cost_model.sharing: Finite vectors materialize intermediate Costed results once; indexed reads and parameter access are free in the arithmetic counter.
cost_model.excluded: This proves an arithmetic-operation bound for the specified shared schedule, not compiled Lean wall-clock time, bit complexity, floating-point stability, measured accelerator runtime or attribution quality. The old recursive expression evaluator itself is not claimed to satisfy this bound.
